title: Reverse Linked List
description:
A singly linked chain is supplied as head. Reverse its links and return the new head. The output contains exactly the input values in reverse traversal order; an empty input [] returns a null head (null output). Change the links rather than merely describing the reversed values.

Each node has a value and a next pointer. The last node in the incoming chain becomes the first node in the returned chain, and the old first node must terminate the result. A single node remains unchanged. Node values can repeat and can be negative, so values alone are not suitable for locating a node.

The interesting part is preserving the unprocessed suffix while changing a pointer: once a link is reversed, its original direction no longer leads to the remaining nodes. An iterative solution can keep the previous and next nodes explicitly, using constant extra memory.

Example 1:

Input: head = [1,2,3]
Output: [3,2,1]

Example 2:

Input: head = []
Output: null

Example 3:

Input: head = [7]
Output: [7]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= number of nodes <= 10,000.
  • -10,000 <= node.val <= 10,000.
